openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Conference registration API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/02_design/*` · Agent: writes.
    Public endpoints (options, settings, registrations) are anonymous and rate limited (SR-03).
    The export is for the organizer role only (BR-08), via HTTP Basic over HTTPS (SR-06).
    Every error body is `application/problem+json` without internal details (ES-07, SB-07).
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: /
tags:
  - name: registration
  - name: organizer
security: []
paths:
  /api/options:
    get:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: listOptions
      summary: Active conference options (AC-003-01)
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Active options only, in configuration order.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/Option"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
  /api/settings:
    get:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: getSettings
      summary: Public form settings (consent wording, anti-automation mode and site key)
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Settings the form needs; contains no secret (AR-07).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Settings"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
  /api/registrations:
    post:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: createRegistration
      summary: Submit a registration (US-001, US-002)
      description: |
        Success is returned only after the database row and the JSON copy are written (AR-05).
        Emails are sent after storage; an email failure does not change the response (D-12).
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Registration accepted.
          headers:
            Location:
              description: Not provided; registrations are not readable through the API.
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationConfirmation"
        "400":
          description: Validation failed, or the anti-automation token was missing or rejected.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationProblem"
        "409":
          description: The email is already registered (D-14); field error on `email`.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationProblem"
        "413":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge"
        "415":
          description: Content type is not `application/json`.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"
  /api/organizer/export:
    get:
      tags: [organizer]
      operationId: exportRegistrations
      summary: Excel export of all registrations (US-008)
      security:
        - organizerBasic: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Workbook with one sheet `Registrations`, one header row and one row per registration.
          headers:
            Content-Disposition:
              description: '`attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`'
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet:
              schema:
                type: string
                contentMediaType: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
        "401":
          description: Missing or wrong organizer credentials; no registration data.
          headers:
            WWW-Authenticate:
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "403":
          description: Organizer access over plain HTTP while HTTPS-only access is on (SR-06).
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
components:
  securitySchemes:
    organizerBasic:
      type: http
      scheme: basic
  responses:
    TooManyRequests:
      description: Rate limit exceeded (SR-03, SB-06).
      headers:
        Retry-After:
          schema:
            type: integer
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
    PayloadTooLarge:
      description: Request body above the configured size limit (SR-03).
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
    ServerError:
      description: Storage failed; nothing was stored and no email was sent (AC-005-03, AC-005-04).
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
  schemas:
    RegistrationType:
      type: string
      enum: [EXTERNAL, STUDENT]
    Category:
      type: string
      enum: [WORKSHOP, EVENT, MEAL, OTHER]
    Option:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name, category, registrationTypes]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$"
        name:
          type: string
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/Category"
        registrationTypes:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
    Settings:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [conferenceName, consent, recaptcha]
      properties:
        conferenceName:
          type: string
        consent:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [id, text]
          properties:
            id:
              type: string
            text:
              type: string
        recaptcha:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [testMode, siteKey]
          properties:
            testMode:
              type: boolean
              description: When true the form shows a test checkbox that yields the test token instead of the Google widget.
            siteKey:
              type: string
              description: Public site key; empty in test mode.
    RegistrationRequest:
      type: object
      description: |
        Text fields are trimmed on the server before validation (BR-02). Field rules (BR-01..BR-05):
        every text field required and at most 200 characters after trimming, email at most 254 and in
        `local@domain.tld` form; EXTERNAL requires `organization` and forbids the student fields;
        STUDENT requires `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` and forbids `organization`.
        `optionIds` holds distinct ids of active options open to the type (D-10, D-13), may be empty.
        `consentGiven` must be true (BR-05). `recaptchaToken` is verified on the server (SR-01).
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [type, firstName, lastName, email, optionIds, consentGiven, recaptchaToken]
      properties:
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
        lastName:
          type: string
        email:
          type: string
        organization:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studyInstitution:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studyProgramme:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studentId:
          type: [string, "null"]
        optionIds:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        consentGiven:
          type: boolean
        recaptchaToken:
          type: string
    SelectedOption:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name, category]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/Category"
    RegistrationConfirmation:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, type, firstName, lastName, email, selectedOptions]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
        lastName:
          type: string
        email:
          type: string
        selectedOptions:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/SelectedOption"
    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [status, title]
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
        status:
          type: integer
        detail:
          type: string
    FieldError:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [field, message]
      properties:
        field:
          type: string
          description: |
            Request property name (`firstName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`,
            `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `optionIds`, `consentGiven`, `recaptchaToken`, `type`).
        message:
          type: string
    ValidationProblem:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        - type: object
          required: [fieldErrors]
          properties:
            fieldErrors:
              type: array
              minItems: 1
              items:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError"

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Conference registration API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    Written in: phase 2 · Source: `docs/01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/02_design/*` · Agent: writes.
    Public endpoints (options, settings, registrations) are anonymous and rate limited (SR-03).
    The export is for the organizer role only (BR-08), via HTTP Basic over HTTPS (SR-06).
    Every error body is `application/problem+json` without internal details (ES-07, SB-07).
  license:
    name: Proprietary
    identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary
servers:
  - url: /
tags:
  - name: registration
  - name: organizer
security: []
paths:
  /api/options:
    get:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: listOptions
      summary: Active conference options (AC-003-01)
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Active options only, in configuration order.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/Option"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
  /api/settings:
    get:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: getSettings
      summary: Public form settings (consent wording, anti-automation mode and site key)
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Settings the form needs; contains no secret (AR-07).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Settings"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
  /api/registrations:
    post:
      tags: [registration]
      operationId: createRegistration
      summary: Submit a registration (US-001, US-002)
      description: |
        Success is returned only after the database row and the JSON copy are written (AR-05).
        Emails are sent after storage; an email failure does not change the response (D-12).
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Registration accepted.
          headers:
            Location:
              description: Not provided; registrations are not readable through the API.
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationConfirmation"
        "400":
          description: Validation failed, or the anti-automation token was missing or rejected.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationProblem"
        "409":
          description: The email is already registered (D-14); field error on `email`.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationProblem"
        "413":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge"
        "415":
          description: Content type is not `application/json`.
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"
  /api/organizer/export:
    get:
      tags: [organizer]
      operationId: exportRegistrations
      summary: Excel export of all registrations (US-008)
      security:
        - organizerBasic: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Workbook with one sheet `Registrations`, one header row and one row per registration.
          headers:
            Content-Disposition:
              description: '`attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`'
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet:
              schema:
                type: string
                contentMediaType: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet
        "401":
          description: Missing or wrong organizer credentials; no registration data.
          headers:
            WWW-Authenticate:
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "403":
          description: Organizer access over plain HTTP while HTTPS-only access is on (SR-06).
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
components:
  securitySchemes:
    organizerBasic:
      type: http
      scheme: basic
  responses:
    TooManyRequests:
      description: Rate limit exceeded (SR-03, SB-06).
      headers:
        Retry-After:
          schema:
            type: integer
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
    PayloadTooLarge:
      description: Request body above the configured size limit (SR-03).
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
    ServerError:
      description: Storage failed; nothing was stored and no email was sent (AC-005-03, AC-005-04).
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
  schemas:
    RegistrationType:
      type: string
      enum: [EXTERNAL, STUDENT]
    Category:
      type: string
      enum: [WORKSHOP, EVENT, MEAL, OTHER]
    Option:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name, category, registrationTypes]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          pattern: "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$"
        name:
          type: string
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/Category"
        registrationTypes:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
    Settings:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [conferenceName, consent, recaptcha]
      properties:
        conferenceName:
          type: string
        consent:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [id, text]
          properties:
            id:
              type: string
            text:
              type: string
        recaptcha:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [testMode, siteKey]
          properties:
            testMode:
              type: boolean
              description: When true the form shows a test checkbox that yields the test token instead of the Google widget.
            siteKey:
              type: string
              description: Public site key; empty in test mode.
    RegistrationRequest:
      type: object
      description: |
        Text fields are trimmed on the server before validation (BR-02). Field rules (BR-01..BR-05):
        every text field required and at most 200 characters after trimming, email at most 254 and in
        `local@domain.tld` form; EXTERNAL requires `organization` and forbids the student fields;
        STUDENT requires `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` and forbids `organization`.
        `optionIds` holds distinct ids of active options open to the type (D-10, D-13), may be empty.
        `consentGiven` must be true (BR-05). `recaptchaToken` is verified on the server (SR-01).
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [type, firstName, lastName, email, optionIds, consentGiven, recaptchaToken]
      properties:
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
        lastName:
          type: string
        email:
          type: string
        organization:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studyInstitution:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studyProgramme:
          type: [string, "null"]
        studentId:
          type: [string, "null"]
        optionIds:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        consentGiven:
          type: boolean
        recaptchaToken:
          type: string
    SelectedOption:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name, category]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/Category"
    RegistrationConfirmation:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, type, firstName, lastName, email, selectedOptions]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
        lastName:
          type: string
        email:
          type: string
        selectedOptions:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/SelectedOption"
    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [status, title]
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
        title:
          type: string
        status:
          type: integer
        detail:
          type: string
    FieldError:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [field, message]
      properties:
        field:
          type: string
          description: |
            Request property name (`firstName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`,
            `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `optionIds`, `consentGiven`, `recaptchaToken`, `type`).
        message:
          type: string
    ValidationProblem:
      allOf:
        - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"
        - type: object
          required: [fieldErrors]
          properties:
            fieldErrors:
              type: array
              minItems: 1
              items:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError"

# Contract: registration storage (PostgreSQL)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, D-14 · Agent: writes

Created only by the Flyway migration `V1__registration.sql` (AR-06, ES-08). Accessed through JPA with bound parameters only (SB-05).

## Table `registration`

| Column | Type | Null | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | no | primary key; generated by the backend |
| `type` | `varchar(16)` | no | `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT` (check constraint) |
| `submitted_at` | `timestamptz` | no | server time of acceptance |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `varchar(200)` | no | trimmed |
| `email` | `varchar(254)` | no | trimmed, as entered |
| `email_normalized` | `varchar(254)` | no | `lower(trim(email))`; **unique** (D-14) |
| `organization` | `varchar(200)` | yes | EXTERNAL only |
| `study_institution`, `study_programme`, `student_id` | `varchar(200)` | yes | STUDENT only |
| `consent_id` | `varchar(64)` | no | |
| `consent_text` | `varchar(1000)` | no | wording shown when the consent was given |
| `consent_given_at` | `timestamptz` | no | |

## Table `registration_option`

| Column | Type | Null | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `registration_id` | `uuid` | no | FK → `registration.id`, on delete cascade |
| `position` | `integer` | no | order of selection; PK (`registration_id`, `position`) |
| `option_id` | `varchar(64)` | no | unique per registration |
| `option_name` | `varchar(200)` | no | display name at acceptance time (survives later configuration changes) |
| `category` | `varchar(16)` | no | `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL`, `OTHER` |

## Write order (AR-05)

1. In one transaction: insert the rows and flush; write the JSON copy to a temporary file in `JSON_COPY_DIR` and move it atomically to `<id>.json`; commit.
2. If the JSON copy fails, the transaction rolls back. If the commit fails, the JSON copy is deleted.
3. Only then are emails sent and the success response returned.
EOF
cat > emails.md <<'EOF'
# Contract: emails (SMTP)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, D-12 · Agent: writes

Sent after the registration is stored (AR-05), one message per recipient, by Spring Mail (Jakarta Mail) to `MAIL_HOST`:`MAIL_PORT` (STARTTLS when `MAIL_TLS=true`). Bodies are `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` only, so user input cannot add markup (SR-05). User input never goes into a header: subjects are fixed text plus the configured conference name, and the only address taken from input is the validated participant email (no CR, LF or comma possible after validation). A failed send is logged as `email failed kind=<PARTICIPANT|ORGANIZER> registration=<id>` without personal data and is not retried (D-12).

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

- From: `MAIL_FROM`; To: the participant's email.
- Subject: `Registration confirmation – <CONFERENCE_NAME>`
- Body (UTF-8 text), in this order: greeting with first and last name; registration type (`External participant` or `Student`); registration id; the selected options grouped by category with display names, or `No optional activities selected.`

## Organizer notification (US-007)

- From: `MAIL_FROM`; To: each address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, one message each.
- Subject: `New registration – <External participant|Student> – <CONFERENCE_NAME>`
- Body: every field of the registration with its label (the same fields as the JSON copy, SR-07), the selected options and the consent timestamp.
- Attachment: `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json`, byte-identical to the JSON copy (AC-007-02).
EOF
cat > anti-automation.md <<'EOF'
# Contract: anti-automation (Google reCAPTCHA v2)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: SR-01, SR-02, AR-07, `environments.md` · Agent: writes

## Frontend

- `GET /api/settings` → `recaptcha.testMode`, `recaptcha.siteKey`. The site key is the frontend's only key and comes from backend configuration (AR-07).
- Live mode: the form loads `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js` and renders the checkbox widget with the site key; the token from the widget is sent as `recaptchaToken`.
- Test mode: no Google script is loaded; the form shows a checkbox labelled `I am not a robot (test mode)`; checking it sets the token to `test-mode-pass`.
- Without a token the form does not submit and shows `Please confirm you are not a robot.`

## Backend

- Every `POST /api/registrations` is verified on the server (SR-01); a missing, blank or rejected token gives 400 with a field error on `recaptchaToken`.
- Live mode: `POST <RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL>` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`), form fields `secret`, `response`, `remoteip`; accepted only when the JSON answer has `"success": true`. A timeout (5 s) or error answer counts as rejected. The URL is configurable so tests run the production path against a mocked endpoint (DoD-P05).
- Test mode (`RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, deterministic): accepts exactly the token `test-mode-pass`, rejects every other token, makes no network call.
- Startup (SR-02): test mode is off unless configured. With test mode off, empty `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` or `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` stops the startup. With the `prod` profile active, test mode on stops the startup.
EOF
cat > ui-form.md <<'EOF'
# Contract: registration form (UI)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, D-11, D-17 · Agent: writes

Single page served at `/`. Language: English (D-17). Tests address elements by role and accessible name, as listed here.

## Choosing the form

Two radio buttons in a group named `Registration type`: `External participant` (selected by default) and `Student`.

## Fields (labels are the accessible names)

| Form | Label | Request field |
|---|---|---|
| both | `First name` | `firstName` |
| both | `Last name` | `lastName` |
| both | `Email` | `email` |
| External participant | `Organization / institution` | `organization` |
| Student | `Study institution` | `studyInstitution` |
| Student | `Study programme` | `studyProgramme` |
| Student | `Student ID` | `studentId` |

The form shows only the fields of the selected type.

## Options

One group per category with a heading `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, in that order; a group without options open to the selected type is not shown. Each option is a checkbox labelled with its display name. Only options from `GET /api/options` whose `registrationTypes` contain the selected type are shown (D-10). Switching type clears selections not open to the new type.

## Consent and anti-automation

- One checkbox labelled with the configured consent text, unchecked on load and after switching type (BR-05).
- Anti-automation as in `anti-automation.md`.

## Submit and errors

- Button `Register`. On press the form validates first (NFR-03): every required field non-blank (`This field is required.`), email format (`Enter a valid email address.`), consent (`Please give your consent.`), token. If any check fails, nothing is sent and each message is shown next to its field (element with `role="alert"` referenced by the field's `aria-describedby`).
- While the request is pending the button is disabled and labelled `Sending…`; no confirmation is shown (AC-004-03).
- 400/409 with `fieldErrors`: each message is shown next to its field; entered values stay (AC-001-16). Errors on `optionIds` and `recaptchaToken` show above the `Register` button.
- Other failures (network, 413, 429, 5xx): a form-level alert `Your registration could not be sent. Please try again.`; entered values stay (AC-004-02).

## Confirmation (US-004)

Shown only after a 201 response (BR-06), replacing the form: heading `Registration received`, the text `Thank you, <first name> <last name>. A confirmation has been sent to <email>.`, and a list of the selected option names (or `No optional activities selected.`).
EOF

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts in `docs/02_contracts/`: `openapi.yaml` (REST), `conference-options.schema.json` (configuration), `registration-copy.schema.json` (JSON copy), `database.md` (SQL), `emails.md` (SMTP), `anti-automation.md` (reCAPTCHA), `ui-form.md` (UI). Versions are only in `tech-stack.md`.

## S1. Components

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot 4 (Java 21) jar in an `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` (uid 1000) | PostgreSQL (JPA), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify URL, JSON copy volume |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite; static files in an `nginx` image, non-root, port 8080 | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| database | `postgres` image | named volume `db-data` | |
| mail catcher | `axllent/mailpit` (local and tests only) | SMTP 1025, API 8025 | |

`02_output/docker-compose.yml` runs all four locally on `127.0.0.1` (frontend `127.0.0.1:8080`, Mailpit UI `127.0.0.1:8025`). The frontend nginx forwards `/api/` to the backend, so the browser uses one origin locally, as the external reverse proxy does in production (`environments.md`).

## S2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Declared style: **layered with ports**. Root package `si.konferenca.registration`.

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model (`Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `Category`, `ConferenceOption`, `OptionCatalog`, `Consent`), validation rules and normalisation (BR-01..BR-05) | Java SE only (no Spring, JPA, servlet, mail, POI) |
| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `ExportService`) and port interfaces (`RegistrationStore`, `RegistrationCopyWriter`, `Notifier`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring transaction annotations |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate-limit and size-limit filters | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` adapter | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.jsoncopy` | `RegistrationCopyWriter` adapter (file system) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.mail` | `Notifier` adapter (Spring Mail) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.captcha` | `CaptchaVerifier` adapters (live, test mode) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.export` | `WorkbookWriter` adapter (Apache POI) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | Spring configuration, `@ConfigurationProperties`, security, option catalog loading, startup guards | any package |

Why: the business rules sit in a framework-free core that unit tests reach directly; each external system (database, file, SMTP, Google, Excel) is behind a port, so acceptance tests can replace one at the boundary (for example a failing copy writer for AC-005-03) without touching the core.

ArchUnit rules (phase 3 acceptance level, `architecture` tests): the dependency table above as a layered architecture; `domain` has no dependency on `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `jakarta.servlet..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..`; infrastructure packages do not depend on each other or on `web`; no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `si.konferenca.registration.infrastructure.(*)..`, AR-03).

## S3. REST API (AR-01)

As in `openapi.yaml`:

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/options` | public, rate limited | active options with `registrationTypes` (AC-003-01) |
| `GET /api/settings` | public, rate limited | conference name, consent id and wording, reCAPTCHA mode and site key |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited | S4 validation → S6 storage → S7 emails → `201` |
| `GET /api/organizer/export` | organizer (S9) | Excel workbook (S9) |
| `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not routed by the proxy | S12 |

Every other path under `/api` answers 404; error bodies are `application/problem+json` with a fixed title per status and no stack trace, exception message or class name (ES-07, SB-07). Status mapping: validation and token → 400 with `fieldErrors`; duplicate email → 409 with `fieldErrors[email]`; malformed JSON → 400 without `fieldErrors` details beyond `body`; body above limit → 413; wrong content type → 415; rate limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; storage failure → 500.

## S4. Validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Done in `domain` on the server for every request, whatever the client did (SB-01). The frontend repeats the field checks for usability only (NFR-03).

1. Trim every text field (BR-02); `null` and blank become missing.
2. `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
3. Required per type (BR-01): both: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; EXTERNAL: `organization`; STUDENT: `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Fields of the other type must be absent or blank → field error `Not allowed for this registration type.`. Message for missing: `This field is required.`
4. Length after trimming: text ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-18) → `Must be at most N characters.` Control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) are rejected in every field → `Contains characters that are not allowed.` Any other Unicode is accepted unchanged (BR-03, NFR-01).
5. Email (BR-03): `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` → `Enter a valid email address.`
6. Options (BR-04, SR-04, D-10, D-13): each id must exist in the configured catalog, be active, and be open to the type; no id twice. Otherwise one field error on `optionIds`: `Unknown, inactive or unavailable option: <id>` or `Option selected more than once: <id>`. The id is echoed only if it matches the identifier pattern; otherwise `Unknown option.`
7. Consent (BR-05): `consentGiven` must be `true` → `Consent is required.`
8. All field errors are collected and returned together (400). The token is verified (S8) only when 1–7 pass, so invalid requests cost no Google call.
9. Duplicate email (D-14): `lower(trim(email))` already stored → 409, field error `This email address is already registered.` Checked before insert and enforced by the unique index (a concurrent duplicate also gives 409).

## S5. Conference options (AR-04, US-003, BR-01)

- Mechanism: a JSON file validated against `conference-options.schema.json`, loaded once at startup from `OPTIONS_LOCATION` (Spring resource: `file:` or `classpath:`). Change = edit the file and restart (D-20). No code or participant field depends on it.
- Startup validation (AC-003-03): schema violations (unknown category, bad id, missing name) and duplicate ids stop the startup with a message naming the option index and id. Implemented by the `config` loader; the failure message never contains other configuration values.
- `registrationTypes` absent = both types (D-10).
- Default `classpath:conference-options.json` is allowed only in local and test; the `prod` profile requires `OPTIONS_LOCATION` to start with `file:` (startup guard).
- The consent id and wording also come from this file (D-11).

## S6. Storage and JSON copy (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

- Schema and write order: `database.md`. Migration `V1__registration.sql` via Flyway; Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`.
- `RegistrationService.register` is one transaction: insert (flush) → write JSON copy (temp file + atomic move to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, UTF-8, content per `registration-copy.schema.json`) → commit. A copy failure throws and rolls back (AC-005-03); a commit failure deletes the copy (AC-005-04). The response is sent only after both (AR-05).
- `JSON_COPY_DIR` must exist and be writable at startup (readiness fails otherwise). Files are created with owner-only permissions (`rw-------`).
- Persistence across container recreation (NFR-02): named volumes `db-data` and `registration-copies`.

## S7. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, D-12)

As in `emails.md`. Sent synchronously after the commit by `Notifier`; each send is wrapped so a failure is logged (id and kind only) and swallowed (AC-006-04). SMTP connection and read timeouts 5 s. No email for a rejected registration (AC-006-05), because emails happen only after a successful commit.

## S8. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07)

As in `anti-automation.md`. `CaptchaVerifier` has two adapters selected by `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`: live (Spring `RestClient` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL`, 5 s timeouts, client IP from the request after the trusted-proxy rules of S10) and test (`test-mode-pass` only). Startup guards: test mode off + empty keys → stop; `prod` profile + test mode on → stop.

## S9. Organizer access and export (US-008, BR-08, SB-02, SB-03, SR-06, SR-07)

- Spring Security, HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` with role `ORGANIZER`; the password is BCrypt-hashed at startup and the plain value is not kept in any bean (SB-03). Empty username or password stops the startup. Sessions: stateless; CSRF off (no cookies, no browser session).
- Only `/api/organizer/**` requires the role; every other path is `permitAll` as listed in S3 (SB-02).
- SR-06: with `ORGANIZER_REQUIRE_HTTPS=true` (default) a request to `/api/organizer/**` that is not secure (scheme after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and does not come from a loopback address gets 403 before authentication, so the credentials are never checked over plain HTTP. Local compose sets it to `false` (plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only).
- Failed organizer logins count against the export rate limit (SB-06).
- Workbook (Apache POI `XSSFWorkbook`): sheet `Registrations`; header row `Registration ID`, `Type`, `Submitted at`, `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, `Consent`, `Consent given at`; one row per registration ordered by submission time; options as display names joined by `; `; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC. Every value is written as a string cell (never a formula), so text starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` stays text (AC-008-05, SB-05). Only these columns are written (SR-07). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## S10. Cross-cutting security (SB, SR)

| Control | Design |
|---|---|
| Rate limits (SB-06, SR-03) | Servlet filter, fixed window per client IP, in memory: `POST /api/registrations` `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATIONS_PER_MINUTE` (default 10); `GET /api/options` and `/api/settings` `RATE_LIMIT_READS_PER_MINUTE` (default 120); `/api/organizer/**` incl. failed logins `RATE_LIMIT_ORGANIZER_PER_MINUTE` (default 10) → 429 (D-19). Client IP: `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` with Tomcat's default internal-proxy ranges, so `X-Forwarded-For` counts only when it comes from the reverse proxy. |
| Request size (SR-03) | Filter rejects bodies above `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413, by `Content-Length` and by counting streamed bytes. |
| Security headers (SB-10) | Backend: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, plus the same nosniff, framing and referrer headers. |
| CORS | Off unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` lists origins (local only); never `*`. |
| Output encoding (SB-05) | JSON by Jackson; React escapes text; emails plain text; Excel string cells; SQL via JPA bound parameters only. |
| Logs (ES-07, SB-07) | Log registration id, status and kind only; never names, emails, tokens, credentials or request bodies. Spring's request logging and SQL parameter logging stay off. |
| TLS (SB-04) | Terminated by the external reverse proxy in production; SMTP uses STARTTLS when `MAIL_TLS=true`; reCAPTCHA over HTTPS. Local runs on 127.0.0.1 only. |
| Least privilege (SB-11) | Both images run as non-root users; compose drops all capabilities and sets `no-new-privileges`; ports bound to 127.0.0.1. |
| Dependencies and source (SB-08, SB-09) | Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6. |
| Secrets (ES-01, ES-02, SB-03) | Only from environment variables; no default value for any secret in code or properties. |

## S11. Configuration (ES-01)

| Variable | Default | Allowed default in | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration` | local, test | `prod` profile has no default |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `registration` | local, test | `prod` profile has no default |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | — | |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_TLS` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false` | local, test | `prod` profile: no default for host and port, `MAIL_TLS` default `true` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty (secret) | — | production only |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.local` | all | |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | all | |
| `OPTIONS_LOCATION` | `classpath:conference-options.json` | local, test | S5 |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `/data/registrations` | all | persistent volume |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | all | `true` only in test and local |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secret) | — | required unless test mode |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | all | |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | — | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none | — | comma separated |
| `ORGANIZER_REQUIRE_HTTPS` | `true` | all | `false` only locally |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | empty | all | |
| `RATE_LIMIT_*`, `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | as in S10 | all | |
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | none | — | `prod` in production |

## S12. Health and operations (ES-09, NFR-04)

Actuator exposes only `health` with liveness and readiness groups; readiness includes the database and the JSON copy directory check. Container health checks: backend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness`; frontend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz` (nginx static `ok`). Compose starts the backend after PostgreSQL is healthy and the frontend after the backend is healthy.

## S13. Frontend (US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07)

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts in `docs/02_contracts/`: `openapi.yaml` (REST), `conference-options.schema.json` (configuration), `registration-copy.schema.json` (JSON copy), `database.md` (SQL), `emails.md` (SMTP), `anti-automation.md` (reCAPTCHA), `ui-form.md` (UI). Versions are only in `tech-stack.md`.

## S1. Components

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot 4 (Java 21) jar in an `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` (uid 1000) | PostgreSQL (JPA), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify URL, JSON copy volume |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite; static files in an `nginx` image, non-root, port 8080 | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| database | `postgres` image | named volume `db-data` | |
| mail catcher | `axllent/mailpit` (local and tests only) | SMTP 1025, API 8025 | |

`02_output/docker-compose.yml` runs all four locally on `127.0.0.1` (frontend `127.0.0.1:8080`, Mailpit UI `127.0.0.1:8025`). The frontend nginx forwards `/api/` to the backend, so the browser uses one origin locally, as the external reverse proxy does in production (`environments.md`).

## S2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Declared style: **layered with ports**. Root package `si.konferenca.registration`.

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | registration model (`Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `Category`, `ConferenceOption`, `OptionCatalog`, `Consent`), validation rules and normalisation (BR-01..BR-05) | Java SE only (no Spring, JPA, servlet, mail, POI) |
| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `ExportService`) and port interfaces (`RegistrationStore`, `RegistrationCopyWriter`, `Notifier`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring transaction annotations |
| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate-limit and size-limit filters | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` adapter | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.jsoncopy` | `RegistrationCopyWriter` adapter (file system) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.mail` | `Notifier` adapter (Spring Mail) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.captcha` | `CaptchaVerifier` adapters (live, test mode) | `application`, `domain` |
| `infrastructure.export` | `WorkbookWriter` adapter (Apache POI) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | Spring configuration, `@ConfigurationProperties`, security, option catalog loading, startup guards | any package |

Why: the business rules sit in a framework-free core that unit tests reach directly; each external system (database, file, SMTP, Google, Excel) is behind a port, so acceptance tests can replace one at the boundary (for example a failing copy writer for AC-005-03) without touching the core.

ArchUnit rules (phase 3 acceptance level, `architecture` tests): the dependency table above as a layered architecture; `domain` has no dependency on `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `jakarta.servlet..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..`; infrastructure packages do not depend on each other or on `web`; no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `si.konferenca.registration.infrastructure.(*)..`, AR-03).

## S3. REST API (AR-01)

As in `openapi.yaml`:

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/options` | public, rate limited | active options with `registrationTypes` (AC-003-01) |
| `GET /api/settings` | public, rate limited | conference name, consent id and wording, reCAPTCHA mode and site key |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited | S4 validation → S6 storage → S7 emails → `201` |
| `GET /api/organizer/export` | organizer (S9) | Excel workbook (S9) |
| `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not routed by the proxy | S12 |

Every other path under `/api` answers 404; error bodies are `application/problem+json` with a fixed title per status and no stack trace, exception message or class name (ES-07, SB-07). Status mapping: validation and token → 400 with `fieldErrors`; duplicate email → 409 with `fieldErrors[email]`; malformed JSON → 400 without `fieldErrors` details beyond `body`; body above limit → 413; wrong content type → 415; rate limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; storage failure → 500.

## S4. Validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Done in `domain` on the server for every request, whatever the client did (SB-01). The frontend repeats the field checks for usability only (NFR-03).

1. Trim every text field (BR-02); `null` and blank become missing.
2. `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
3. Required per type (BR-01): both: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; EXTERNAL: `organization`; STUDENT: `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Fields of the other type must be absent or blank → field error `Not allowed for this registration type.`. Message for missing: `This field is required.`
4. Length after trimming: text ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-18) → `Must be at most N characters.` Control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) are rejected in every field → `Contains characters that are not allowed.` Any other Unicode is accepted unchanged (BR-03, NFR-01).
5. Email (BR-03): `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` → `Enter a valid email address.`
6. Options (BR-04, SR-04, D-10, D-13): each id must exist in the configured catalog, be active, and be open to the type; no id twice. Otherwise one field error on `optionIds`: `Unknown, inactive or unavailable option: <id>` or `Option selected more than once: <id>`. The id is echoed only if it matches the identifier pattern; otherwise `Unknown option.`
7. Consent (BR-05): `consentGiven` must be `true` → `Consent is required.`
8. All field errors are collected and returned together (400). The token is verified (S8) only when 1–7 pass, so invalid requests cost no Google call.
9. Duplicate email (D-14): `lower(trim(email))` already stored → 409, field error `This email address is already registered.` Checked before insert and enforced by the unique index (a concurrent duplicate also gives 409).

## S5. Conference options (AR-04, US-003, BR-01)

- Mechanism: a JSON file validated against `conference-options.schema.json`, loaded once at startup from `OPTIONS_LOCATION` (Spring resource: `file:` or `classpath:`). Change = edit the file and restart (D-20). No code or participant field depends on it.
- Startup validation (AC-003-03): schema violations (unknown category, bad id, missing name) and duplicate ids stop the startup with a message naming the option index and id. Implemented by the `config` loader; the failure message never contains other configuration values.
- `registrationTypes` absent = both types (D-10).
- Default `classpath:conference-options.json` is allowed only in local and test; the `prod` profile requires `OPTIONS_LOCATION` to start with `file:` (startup guard).
- The consent id and wording also come from this file (D-11).

## S6. Storage and JSON copy (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

- Schema and write order: `database.md`. Migration `V1__registration.sql` via Flyway; Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`.
- `RegistrationService.register` is one transaction: insert (flush) → write JSON copy (temp file + atomic move to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, UTF-8, content per `registration-copy.schema.json`) → commit. A copy failure throws and rolls back (AC-005-03); a commit failure deletes the copy (AC-005-04). The response is sent only after both (AR-05).
- `JSON_COPY_DIR` must exist and be writable at startup (readiness fails otherwise). Files are created with owner-only permissions (`rw-------`).
- Persistence across container recreation (NFR-02): named volumes `db-data` and `registration-copies`.

## S7. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, D-12)

As in `emails.md`. Sent synchronously after the commit by `Notifier`; each send is wrapped so a failure is logged (id and kind only) and swallowed (AC-006-04). SMTP connection and read timeouts 5 s. No email for a rejected registration (AC-006-05), because emails happen only after a successful commit.

## S8. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07)

As in `anti-automation.md`. `CaptchaVerifier` has two adapters selected by `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`: live (Spring `RestClient` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL`, 5 s timeouts, client IP from the request after the trusted-proxy rules of S10) and test (`test-mode-pass` only). Startup guards: test mode off + empty keys → stop; `prod` profile + test mode on → stop.

## S9. Organizer access and export (US-008, BR-08, SB-02, SB-03, SR-06, SR-07)

- Spring Security, HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` with role `ORGANIZER`; the password is BCrypt-hashed at startup and the plain value is not kept in any bean (SB-03). Empty username or password stops the startup. Sessions: stateless; CSRF off (no cookies, no browser session).
- Only `/api/organizer/**` requires the role; every other path is `permitAll` as listed in S3 (SB-02).
- SR-06: with `ORGANIZER_REQUIRE_HTTPS=true` (default) a request to `/api/organizer/**` that is not secure (scheme after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and does not come from a loopback address gets 403 before authentication, so the credentials are never checked over plain HTTP. Local compose sets it to `false` (plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only).
- Failed organizer logins count against the export rate limit (SB-06).
- Workbook (Apache POI `XSSFWorkbook`): sheet `Registrations`; header row `Registration ID`, `Type`, `Submitted at`, `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, `Consent`, `Consent given at`; one row per registration ordered by submission time; options as display names joined by `; `; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC. Every value is written as a string cell (never a formula), so text starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` stays text (AC-008-05, SB-05). Only these columns are written (SR-07). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## S10. Cross-cutting security (SB, SR)

| Control | Design |
|---|---|
| Rate limits (SB-06, SR-03) | Servlet filter, fixed window per client IP, in memory: `POST /api/registrations` `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATIONS_PER_MINUTE` (default 10); `GET /api/options` and `/api/settings` `RATE_LIMIT_READS_PER_MINUTE` (default 120); `/api/organizer/**` incl. failed logins `RATE_LIMIT_ORGANIZER_PER_MINUTE` (default 10) → 429 (D-19). Client IP: `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` with Tomcat's default internal-proxy ranges, so `X-Forwarded-For` counts only when it comes from the reverse proxy. |
| Request size (SR-03) | Filter rejects bodies above `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413, by `Content-Length` and by counting streamed bytes. |
| Security headers (SB-10) | Backend: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, plus the same nosniff, framing and referrer headers. |
| CORS | Off unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` lists origins (local only); never `*`. |
| Output encoding (SB-05) | JSON by Jackson; React escapes text; emails plain text; Excel string cells; SQL via JPA bound parameters only. |
| Logs (ES-07, SB-07) | Log registration id, status and kind only; never names, emails, tokens, credentials or request bodies. Spring's request logging and SQL parameter logging stay off. |
| TLS (SB-04) | Terminated by the external reverse proxy in production; SMTP uses STARTTLS when `MAIL_TLS=true`; reCAPTCHA over HTTPS. Local runs on 127.0.0.1 only. |
| Least privilege (SB-11) | Both images run as non-root users; compose drops all capabilities and sets `no-new-privileges`; ports bound to 127.0.0.1. |
| Dependencies and source (SB-08, SB-09) | Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6. |
| Secrets (ES-01, ES-02, SB-03) | Only from environment variables; no default value for any secret in code or properties. |

## S11. Configuration (ES-01)

| Variable | Default | Allowed default in | Notes |

| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration` | local, test | `prod` profile has no default |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `registration` | local, test | `prod` profile has no default |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | — | |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_TLS` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false` | local, test | `prod` profile: no default for host and port, `MAIL_TLS` default `true` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty (secret) | — | production only |

| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | all | `true` only in test and local |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secret) | — | required unless test mode |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | all | |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secret) | — | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none | — | comma separated |
| `ORGANIZER_REQUIRE_HTTPS` | `true` | all | `false` only locally |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | empty | all | |
| `RATE_LIMIT_*`, `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | as in S10 | all | |
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | none | — | `prod` in production |

| `infrastructure.jsoncopy` | `RegistrationCopyWriter` adapter (file system) | `application`, `domain` |

Why: the business rules sit in a framework-free core that unit tests reach directly; each external system (database, file, SMTP, Google, Excel) is behind a port, so acceptance tests can replace one at the boundary (for example a failing copy writer for AC-005-03) without touching the core.

ArchUnit rules (phase 3 acceptance level, `architecture` tests): the dependency table above as a layered architecture; `domain` has no dependency on `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `jakarta.servlet..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..`; infrastructure packages do not depend on each other or on `web`; no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `si.konferenca.registration.infrastructure.(*)..`, AR-03).

## S3. REST API (AR-01)

As in `openapi.yaml`:

| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/options` | public, rate limited | active options with `registrationTypes` (AC-003-01) |
| `GET /api/settings` | public, rate limited | conference name, consent id and wording, reCAPTCHA mode and site key |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited | S4 validation → S6 storage → S7 emails → `201` |
| `GET /api/organizer/export` | organizer (S9) | Excel workbook (S9) |
| `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not routed by the proxy | S12 |

Every other path under `/api` answers 404; error bodies are `application/problem+json` with a fixed title per status and no stack trace, exception message or class name (ES-07, SB-07). Status mapping: validation and token → 400 with `fieldErrors`; duplicate email → 409 with `fieldErrors[email]`; malformed JSON → 400 without `fieldErrors` details beyond `body`; body above limit → 413; wrong content type → 415; rate limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; storage failure → 500.

## S4. Validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)

Done in `domain` on the server for every request, whatever the client did (SB-01). The frontend repeats the field checks for usability only (NFR-03).

1. Trim every text field (BR-02); `null` and blank become missing.
2. `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
3. Required per type (BR-01): both: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; EXTERNAL: `organization`; STUDENT: `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Fields of the other type must be absent or blank → field error `Not allowed for this registration type.`. Message for missing: `This field is required.`
4. Length after trimming: text ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-18) → `Must be at most N characters.` Control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) are rejected in every field → `Contains characters that are not allowed.` Any other Unicode is accepted unchanged (BR-03, NFR-01).
5. Email (BR-03): `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` → `Enter a valid email address.`
6. Options (BR-04, SR-04, D-10, D-13): each id must exist in the configured catalog, be active, and be open to the type; no id twice. Otherwise one field error on `optionIds`: `Unknown, inactive or unavailable option: <id>` or `Option selected more than once: <id>`. The id is echoed only if it matches the identifier pattern; otherwise `Unknown option.`
7. Consent (BR-05): `consentGiven` must be `true` → `Consent is required.`
8. All field errors are collected and returned together (400). The token is verified (S8) only when 1–7 pass, so invalid requests cost no Google call.
9. Duplicate email (D-14): `lower(trim(email))` already stored → 409, field error `This email address is already registered.` Checked before insert and enforced by the unique index (a concurrent duplicate also gives 409).

## S5. Conference options (AR-04, US-003, BR-01)

- Mechanism: a JSON file validated against `conference-options.schema.json`, loaded once at startup from `OPTIONS_LOCATION` (Spring resource: `file:` or `classpath:`). Change = edit the file and restart (D-20). No code or participant field depends on it.
- Startup validation (AC-003-03): schema violations (unknown category, bad id, missing name) and duplicate ids stop the startup with a message naming the option index and id. Implemented by the `config` loader; the failure message never contains other configuration values.
- `registrationTypes` absent = both types (D-10).
- Default `classpath:conference-options.json` is allowed only in local and test; the `prod` profile requires `OPTIONS_LOCATION` to start with `file:` (startup guard).
- The consent id and wording also come from this file (D-11).

## S6. Storage and JSON copy (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

- Schema and write order: `database.md`. Migration `V1__registration.sql` via Flyway; Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate`.
- `RegistrationService.register` is one transaction: insert (flush) → write JSON copy (temp file + atomic move to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, UTF-8, content per `registration-copy.schema.json`) → commit. A copy failure throws and rolls back (AC-005-03); a commit failure deletes the copy (AC-005-04). The response is sent only after both (AR-05).
- `JSON_COPY_DIR` must exist and be writable at startup (readiness fails otherwise). Files are created with owner-only permissions (`rw-------`).
- Persistence across container recreation (NFR-02): named volumes `db-data` and `registration-copies`.

## S7. Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, D-12)

As in `emails.md`. Sent synchronously after the commit by `Notifier`; each send is wrapped so a failure is logged (id and kind only) and swallowed (AC-006-04). SMTP connection and read timeouts 5 s. No email for a rejected registration (AC-006-05), because emails happen only after a successful commit.

## S8. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07)

As in `anti-automation.md`. `CaptchaVerifier` has two adapters selected by `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`: live (Spring `RestClient` to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL`, 5 s timeouts, client IP from the request after the trusted-proxy rules of S10) and test (`test-mode-pass` only). Startup guards: test mode off + empty keys → stop; `prod` profile + test mode on → stop.

## S9. Organizer access and export (US-008, BR-08, SB-02, SB-03, SR-06, SR-07)

- Spring Security, HTTP Basic, one in-memory user from `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` with role `ORGANIZER`; the password is BCrypt-hashed at startup and the plain value is not kept in any bean (SB-03). Empty username or password stops the startup. Sessions: stateless; CSRF off (no cookies, no browser session).
- Only `/api/organizer/**` requires the role; every other path is `permitAll` as listed in S3 (SB-02).
- SR-06: with `ORGANIZER_REQUIRE_HTTPS=true` (default) a request to `/api/organizer/**` that is not secure (scheme after `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted proxy) and does not come from a loopback address gets 403 before authentication, so the credentials are never checked over plain HTTP. Local compose sets it to `false` (plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only).
- Failed organizer logins count against the export rate limit (SB-06).
- Workbook (Apache POI `XSSFWorkbook`): sheet `Registrations`; header row `Registration ID`, `Type`, `Submitted at`, `First name`, `Last name`, `Email`, `Organization / institution`, `Study institution`, `Study programme`, `Student ID`, `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`, `Consent`, `Consent given at`; one row per registration ordered by submission time; options as display names joined by `; `; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC. Every value is written as a string cell (never a formula), so text starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` stays text (AC-008-05, SB-05). Only these columns are written (SR-07). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## S10. Cross-cutting security (SB, SR)

| Control | Design |
|---|---|
| Rate limits (SB-06, SR-03) | Servlet filter, fixed window per client IP, in memory: `POST /api/registrations` `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATIONS_PER_MINUTE` (default 10); `GET /api/options` and `/api/settings` `RATE_LIMIT_READS_PER_MINUTE` (default 120); `/api/organizer/**` incl. failed logins `RATE_LIMIT_ORGANIZER_PER_MINUTE` (default 10) → 429 (D-19). Client IP: `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` with Tomcat's default internal-proxy ranges, so `X-Forwarded-For` counts only when it comes from the reverse proxy. |
| Request size (SR-03) | Filter rejects bodies above `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 16384) → 413, by `Content-Length` and by counting streamed bytes. |
| Security headers (SB-10) | Backend: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, plus the same nosniff, framing and referrer headers. |
| CORS | Off unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` lists origins (local only); never `*`. |
| Output encoding (SB-05) | JSON by Jackson; React escapes text; emails plain text; Excel string cells; SQL via JPA bound parameters only. |
| Logs (ES-07, SB-07) | Log registration id, status and kind only; never names, emails, tokens, credentials or request bodies. Spring's request logging and SQL parameter logging stay off. |
| TLS (SB-04) | Terminated by the external reverse proxy in production; SMTP uses STARTTLS when `MAIL_TLS=true`; reCAPTCHA over HTTPS. Local runs on 127.0.0.1 only. |
| Least privilege (SB-11) | Both images run as non-root users; compose drops all capabilities and sets `no-new-privileges`; ports bound to 127.0.0.1. |
| Dependencies and source (SB-08, SB-09) | Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6. |
| Secrets (ES-01, ES-02, SB-03) | Only from environment variables; no default value for any secret in code or properties. |

## S12. Health and operations (ES-09, NFR-04)

Actuator exposes only `health` with liveness and readiness groups; readiness includes the database and the JSON copy directory check. Container health checks: backend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness`; frontend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz` (nginx static `ok`). Compose starts the backend after PostgreSQL is healthy and the frontend after the backend is healthy.

## S13. Frontend (US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07)

React function components, no router. `App` loads `/api/settings` and `/api/options`, then renders `RegistrationForm` (behaviour in `ui-form.md`) and, after a 201, `Confirmation`. A small `api.ts` wraps `fetch` for the three endpoints and maps 400/409 `fieldErrors`. Client validation mirrors S4 steps 1, 3, 5 and 7 and the token; the backend stays authoritative. No secret and no backend URL in the bundle: relative `/api` paths only (AR-01, AR-07). Text is rendered through React (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`).

## S14. Personal data (SB-12, SB-13, SB-14)

Collected: exactly the fields of BR-01 plus selected options and consent with timestamp, as in `security-requirements.md`; no IP address or token is stored (the IP is used in memory only for rate limiting and the Google verify call). Retention (D-15): until 12 months after the conference, deleted manually by the organizer (release notes). Consent (D-11): explicit, unchecked by default, wording and timestamp stored.

## S15. Test approach (summary; detail in phase 3)

| Level | Tool | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| acceptance (backend) | JUnit 6, Spring Boot test on a random port, `RestClient`, Testcontainers PostgreSQL and Mailpit | API, storage, JSON copy, emails, export, security, startup guards |
| architecture | ArchUnit | S2 rules, AR-03 |
| acceptance (frontend) | Vitest + Testing Library with a mocked `fetch` | form, client validation, error display, confirmation |
| e2e | Playwright against the compose stack | full flow incl. NFR-01 |

D-16 (Redocly CLI for contract validation), D-17 (English UI), D-18 (field length limits), D-19 (rate-limit defaults), D-20 (option changes need a restart).

+
+## S1. Components
+
+| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot 4 (Java 21) jar in an `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` (uid 1000) | PostgreSQL (JPA), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify URL, JSON copy volume |
+| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React SPA built by Vite; static files in an `nginx` image, non-root, port 8080 | backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |

+
+`02_output/docker-compose.yml` runs all four locally on `127.0.0.1` (frontend `127.0.0.1:8080`, Mailpit UI `127.0.0.1:8025`). The frontend nginx forwards `/api/` to the backend, so the browser uses one origin locally, as the external reverse proxy does in production (`environments.md`).
+
+## S2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)
+
+Declared style: **layered with ports**. Root package `si.konferenca.registration`.
+
+| Package | Holds | May depend on |
+|---|---|---|
+| `domain` | registration model (`Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `Category`, `ConferenceOption`, `OptionCatalog`, `Consent`), validation rules and normalisation (BR-01..BR-05) | Java SE only (no Spring, JPA, servlet, mail, POI) |
+| `application` | use cases (`RegistrationService`, `ExportService`) and port interfaces (`RegistrationStore`, `RegistrationCopyWriter`, `Notifier`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `WorkbookWriter`) | `domain`, Spring transaction annotations |
+| `web` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, rate-limit and size-limit filters | `application`, `domain` |
+| `infrastructure.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` adapter | `application`, `domain` |
+| `infrastructure.jsoncopy` | `RegistrationCopyWriter` adapter (file system) | `application`, `domain` |
+| `infrastructure.mail` | `Notifier` adapter (Spring Mail) | `application`, `domain` |
+| `infrastructure.captcha` | `CaptchaVerifier` adapters (live, test mode) | `application`, `domain` |
+| `infrastructure.export` | `WorkbookWriter` adapter (Apache POI) | `application`, `domain` |
+| `config` | Spring configuration, `@ConfigurationProperties`, security, option catalog loading, startup guards | any package |
+
+Why: the business rules sit in a framework-free core that unit tests reach directly; each external system (database, file, SMTP, Google, Excel) is behind a port, so acceptance tests can replace one at the boundary (for example a failing copy writer for AC-005-03) without touching the core.
+
+ArchUnit rules (phase 3 acceptance level, `architecture` tests): the dependency table above as a layered architecture; `domain` has no dependency on `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `jakarta.servlet..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..`; infrastructure packages do not depend on each other or on `web`; no package cycles (slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `si.konferenca.registration.infrastructure.(*)..`, AR-03).
+
+## S3. REST API (AR-01)
+
+As in `openapi.yaml`:
+
+| Endpoint | Access | Behaviour |
+|---|---|---|
+| `GET /api/options` | public, rate limited | active options with `registrationTypes` (AC-003-01) |
+| `GET /api/settings` | public, rate limited | conference name, consent id and wording, reCAPTCHA mode and site key |
+| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited | S4 validation → S6 storage → S7 emails → `201` |
+| `GET /api/organizer/export` | organizer (S9) | Excel workbook (S9) |
+| `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not routed by the proxy | S12 |
+
+Every other path under `/api` answers 404; error bodies are `application/problem+json` with a fixed title per status and no stack trace, exception message or class name (ES-07, SB-07). Status mapping: validation and token → 400 with `fieldErrors`; duplicate email → 409 with `fieldErrors[email]`; malformed JSON → 400 without `fieldErrors` details beyond `body`; body above limit → 413; wrong content type → 415; rate limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; storage failure → 500.
+
+## S4. Validation (BR-01..BR-05, SB-01, SR-04)
+
+Done in `domain` on the server for every request, whatever the client did (SB-01). The frontend repeats the field checks for usability only (NFR-03).
+
+1. Trim every text field (BR-02); `null` and blank become missing.
+2. `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
+3. Required per type (BR-01): both: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`; EXTERNAL: `organization`; STUDENT: `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`. Fields of the other type must be absent or blank → field error `Not allowed for this registration type.`. Message for missing: `This field is required.`
+4. Length after trimming: text ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-18) → `Must be at most N characters.` Control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) are rejected in every field → `Contains characters that are not allowed.` Any other Unicode is accepted unchanged (BR-03, NFR-01).
+5. Email (BR-03): `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` → `Enter a valid email address.`
+6. Options (BR-04, SR-04, D-10, D-13): each id must exist in the configured catalog, be active, and be open to the type; no id twice. Otherwise one field error on `optionIds`: `Unknown, inactive or unavailable option: <id>` or `Option selected more than once: <id>`. The id is echoed only if it matches the identifier pattern; otherwise `Unknown option.`
+7. Consent (BR-05): `consentGiven` must be `true` → `Consent is required.`
+8. All field errors are collected and returned together (400). The token is verified (S8) only when 1–7 pass, so invalid requests cost no Google call.
+9. Duplicate email (D-14): `lower(trim(email))` already stored → 409, field error `This email address is already registered.` Checked before insert and enforced by the unique index (a concurrent duplicate also gives 409).

+- Startup validation (AC-003-03): schema violations (unknown category, bad id, missing name) and duplicate ids stop the startup with a message naming the option index and id. Implemented by the `config` loader; the failure message never contains other configuration values.
+- `registrationTypes` absent = both types (D-10).
+- Default `classpath:conference-options.json` is allowed only in local and test; the `prod` profile requires `OPTIONS_LOCATION` to start with `file:` (startup guard).

+- Persistence across container recreation (NFR-02): named volumes `db-data` and `registration-copies`.

No email for a rejected registration (AC-006-05), because emails happen only after a successful commit.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Runs docker compose for the local stack with the keys it needs from the repository's .env,
# without printing them and without parsing any other line of .env.
# Usage (from anywhere): 02_output/scripts/compose.sh up -d --build
set -eu
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
env_file="${ENV_FILE:-$here/../.env}"
for key in POSTGRES_PASSWORD ORGANIZER_USERNAME ORGANIZER_PASSWORD ORGANIZER_EMAILS CONFERENCE_NAME; do
  value="$(sed -n "s/^$key=//p" "$env_file" | tr -d '\r')"
  [ -n "$value" ] && export "$key=$value"
done
exec docker compose -f "$here/docker-compose.yml" "$@"
EOF

## Procedure

1. Re-read the requirements (`project/01_requirements/*`, `docs/01_*`, `docs/02_*`) before checking anything.
2. Recompute every hash in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` and `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`. Any mismatch is a Critical finding, whatever the reason.
3. Run the full test suite and every check command (ES-05); record results, coverage and mutation score exactly as defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.
4. Start every component as described for its target environment and exercise the core user flows at runtime; record what was run and what was observed.
5. Security: for every `SB` and `SR` item, record where it is implemented and how it was checked (test, scan, or inspection). An item without evidence is a finding.
6. Run every scanner listed under `tooling` with a security purpose (dependency, static analysis, secrets); archive raw output in `out/logs/`.
7. Classify each finding with the severity scale. For a dependency vulnerability, check whether the vulnerable feature is used. If you propose lowering a Critical or High on that basis, record the evidence and raise a blocking decision.
8. Check logs and error responses produced during testing for personal data, secrets and internals. Then check that no `.env` value leaked, listing file names only and never the values (no output means clean; any name listed is a Critical finding):

   - commit messages: `git log --all --format=%B | grep -cF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')` (must print `0`)
9. Build the traceability table: AC → tests → commits.
10. For each general and project DoD item, record evidence or a finding.
11. For every Critical or High finding, run verify → fix → re-verify and log each loop; triage Medium and Low as fixed, accepted with a reason, or open item.
12. Confirm every decision record has a resolution or is marked pending review.
13. State at the top of the report that it is a self-check, not an independent review.
